brief.en: Sixty guests filled Surajgarh Haveli for Teej. Between the aarti and the fireworks, Rani-sa’s nine-gem peacock brooch vanished from the puja room. The doors were watched. The window was latched. Somebody inside knows exactly where it went.

iraNote.en: “An anklet says she was there. It doesn’t say when. Check who signs with a V.”

label.en: TORN NOTE · FOUND IN THE PUJA ROOM

text.en: “Meet me at the jharokha after aarti. Don’t be late. — V”

label.en: TRAIN TICKET · TUCKED IN A COAT

text.en: JAIPUR → MUMBAI · 11:40 PM tonight · seat 42 · name left blank
Puja-room skylight latch — broken from the INSIDE.
Fresh ghee smudge on the jewel-box latch. Kitchen-grade.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — every cook in Jaipur has ghee on their hands

text.en: Two lakh due on Teej night. The borrower’s name has been inked over.
One ghungroo from a dancer’s anklet. No way to date the fall.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — it says she was there, not when

text.en: Sixty names. One arrived at 6:50 — an hour into the aarti — and signed with an initial.
Snuffed with a wet cloth, not blown out. Blowing it would have been seen from the courtyard.
A man at the counter at 9:04 in a Kashmiri shawl. The shawl is the only thing in focus.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — half of Jaipur owns that shawl

text.en: A man’s ear stud, third step. Reported lost by the durwan a week earlier.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — he lost it a week ago and said so at the time

hook.en: fetched ghee near the puja room

alibi.en: The ghee was his, the timing was not. He was at the tandoor from 5:30, in front of nine people.

hook.en: her anklet bell, under the jharokha

alibi.en: Her anklet was at the jharokha — but she was performing on stage from 5 to 7. Forty witnesses.

hook.en: arrived late · owes Sethji two lakh

confession.en: Planned to lift the brooch, pay Sethji, and catch the 11:40 to Mumbai.

hook.en: his birds roost above the skylight

alibi.en: His birds broke the skylight latch weeks ago. He was on the roof, and the roof has no way down into the puja room.

hook.en: the two lakh is owed to him

alibi.en: A moneylender wants his money, not a brooch he’d have to sell twice. He was at his counter until midnight, and his counter had a queue.

correction.en: A motive is a debt, not a smudge. Two lakh came due on Teej night.
The anklet says somebody was at the jharokha. The note says who called them there.
Nobody escapes on a broken latch. There was a train at 11:40 with no name on it.

text.en: “On a stage, five until seven. Forty people. Ask any of them.”

dismissNote.en: ruled out — a true alibi clears one person and charges nobody

text.en: “Someone’s been leaving a lamp in the stairwell window at night. A lamp means come up.”
“A private matter, and a settled one.” It came due that night, and Sethji’s book says it was never paid.

setting.en: The green room, still in her ghungroos, one anklet short.

ask.en: When did you lose the bell?

answer.en: “I don’t know. You don’t hear one bell go when there are ninety.”

note.en: So the anklet dates nothing — which is exactly what the lab said about it.

ask.en: A ghungroo under the jharokha. What were you doing there?

answer.en: “I wasn’t. I was on a stage from five until seven and forty people watched me do it.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the anklet bell first. Put the thing in her hand before you put the question.

note.en: Forty witnesses. She is the only person in this house with an alibi you could hang a hat on.

ask.en: Who else was at the jharokha?

answer.en: “Somebody was waiting. I saw a shawl going up the stairs at half six.”

note.en: A shawl on the stairs at half six. The aarti began at half five.

setting.en: The roof, among the pigeons, which he will not come down from.

answer.en: “Weeks ago. I told the durwan and he wrote it in the book.”

note.en: The latch was already broken. So the skylight proves *inside*, not entry.

ask.en: Can a man get from this roof into the puja room?

answer.en: “No. There’s a beam and then there’s a drop. I’ve never done it, and I’m the only one who’d try.”

note.en: Then nobody came down. Whoever took it was already in the house.

ask.en: The latch was broken from the inside. Who else goes up here?

answer.en: “Nobody. But somebody’s been leaving a lamp in the stairwell window at night. A lamp means come up.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the skylight polaroid — the inside break is the whole reason to be on this roof.

note.en: A signal, then. Somebody has been arranging to meet somebody, and not for the first time.

setting.en: The drawing room. He answers with his coat still on.

ask.en: You arrived at ten to seven.

answer.en: “Traffic. Teej traffic. Ask anybody who came from Amber.”

note.en: An hour into the aarti — and he signed the guest book with an initial.

ask.en: Two lakh, due to Sethji on Teej night.

answer.en: “A private matter, and a settled one.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the ledger slip. A debt you have not written down is a rumour, and he does not answer rumours.

note.en: Settled. He says it as though it already were.

ask.en: There is a seat on the 11:40 with no name on it.

answer.en: “A man may hold a ticket. Holding a ticket is not a crime.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the ticket. You cannot put a train to a man from memory.

note.en: No, it isn’t. But a man who booked no name and arrived an hour late is a man with somewhere to be.

bankedClue.en: A note signed “V” — the same hand as the inked-over ledger name

teaser.en: Rani-sa’s nine-gem brooch vanished mid-festival at Surajgarh Haveli. Solve it to unlock the Pink City finale.

text.en: Whoever wrote the note plans to be on that train. Who signs with a V — and booked no name?
